answer: Distinct Ephemeral Sensor Fingerprints assigns each agent a cedar-keyed hardware nonce fused with its sensor noise, so one machine's drift under thermal load diverges from any clone it spawns. During each transaction window, a nebula of timing jitter and analog offsets is measured and matched against the enrolled profile, and mismatches above tolerance void the identity. Replicating the timber of a physical device costs an attacker a full fabrication run per identity, roughly thousands in specialized hardware and weeks of calibration, defeating cheap duplication.
